bearings.paper_claim: MOPBD* returns the exact Pareto-optimal set of source-to-goal paths (Theorem 1: C = C*). Multi-objective shortest path is NP-hard even with two objectives, and the front can grow exponentially with the number of nodes.
bearings.paper_location: Theorem 1 at PDF p.6 (text line 672); NP-hard and exponential statements at PDF p.1 and p.6 (text lines 88-90 and 675-676)
bearings.system_side: Docstring line 3 says RELINK + MOPBD*. The code runs a greedy build_route for each lambda in 0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4 (line 70), scoring candidate edges as (gain - lam(1-p))/cost, then filters (cost, spread, risk) points by dominance (lines 64-76). It is a lambda-parameterised greedy heuristic over recruitment sets, not a weighted sum over the three objectives and not a path search.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper claim concerns source-target paths with additive vector costs. The route finder uses a product-form reach and a mean-p risk over a recruitment set, so MOPBD* cannot be dropped in. The docstring overstates the method; the front is a heuristic approximation, not an exact Pareto set.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper claims and docstring verified. The analyst wording weighted-sum sweep over five fixed risk weights is inaccurate: lambda is a risk penalty inside a greedy value, not a weights vector over objectives. The convex-hull point is a generic weighted-sum property that does not describe this code. Fields corrected.

bearings.paper_claim: Incremental reuse helps when cost changes are few and local. On the maze map with random obstacle add and delete (M = 2, 3, 4; 5 minute limit), MOPBD* beats from-scratch NAMOA* in general on median and average runtime, but its advantage shrinks as M grows and from-scratch NAMOA* wins at M = 4. The worst case can exceed from-scratch search when many states are invalidated.
bearings.paper_location: Sec VI-B at PDF p.6 (highlight on deleted states); Sec VII-D at PDF p.8, Table II (text lines 808-833)
bearings.system_side: cosponsor_route.py keeps no saved search state: each run rebuilds routes from scratch (build_route called fresh for each lambda, lines 41-62 and 70-72). Edge probabilities come from MBC.build_P(adj) over the whole network (around line 22). The statement that these probabilities change in batch at pipeline refresh was not verified from code read here.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper evidence covers single-robot grid planning with local edge changes at 1 to 5 minute limits on simulated grids in Python. It does not cover whole-network batch refresh or changes to global weights such as lambda or K.
bearings.verifier_note: No-state reuse verified in code. The M = 4 crossover and the worst-case caveat are verified in the paper. The analyst reading that MOPBD* beats NAMOA* at M = 2-3 on the maze map is not stated; Table II is maze-only with M = 2, 3, 4 and is described in general terms, and its values are not recoverable from the extraction. The batch-refresh statement is unverified.

bearings.paper_claim: Vector costs with a non-dominated set expose trade-offs that a single scalar sum hides. Epsilon-dominance (0.01 to 0.05) gives smaller stored sets and faster runs, at a cost in solution quality; the paper states no set-size or runtime bound. The advantage over from-scratch search shrinks as the number of objectives grows.
bearings.paper_location: Sec VI-C at PDF p.6-7; Sec VII-B and VII-C at PDF p.7, Fig 3; Sec VII-D at PDF p.8
bearings.system_side: Hop cost is minus log of HOP_FACTOR times strength plus a fixed weight times uncertainty (_hop_cost, lines 115-116). HOP_FACTOR is 0.8 in fec/staffer_network/closeness_math.py:20. Search is bidirectional Dijkstra with heuristic 0 (ALGORITHM, line 79). Yen loopless alternatives follow the same scalar (module docstring, line 23). Ties go to the fewest steps, then the least cost (around line 519).
bearings.transfer_conditions: The extension applies only if the strength-uncertainty trade-off should be shown as a front rather than fixed by w. It would add latency where route speed is already a concern. Any front members remain heuristic model outputs, never closeness or introduction probabilities (D-025).
bearings.verifier_note: Code verified: scalar hop cost, HOP_FACTOR 0.8, bidirectional Dijkstra with heuristic 0, Yen alternatives, tie rule. The paper says epsilon shrinks sets and runtime but gives no bound, so bounds is removed. Two objectives performs best is a reading of the trend across M, not a stated claim, so it is softened to largest advantage at two objectives.
